ratings.comment: One of the most unorganized professors here. Web development is not really that difficult, but his exams are super specific on random topics that we hardly went over. Projects were easy but even then he was unclear as to what he wanted. While this might seem like a fun elective, I highly advise you avoid him if you want a stress free semester.

Sure he is a nice guy, but he really isn't a great lecturer. He will often talk in circles reading off of a pdf at 200% zoom. His exams are intentionally worded poorly to confuse students, his study guides don't reflect the exam content, and exams weigh about 80% of your total grade. He also expects you to do a bunch of ungraded assignments.

this course is super exam heavy since they make up most of your grade but its usually multiple choice scantrons with 50+ questions. its easy to get a B but insanely hard to end with an A here. he curves all exams by adding extra points.

Tests will make up almost 60% of you grade, you can take cheat sheets and for the most part of T/F and MCQ questions. Projects are super easy and will give you credit as long as it runs. Quizzes are in person & sometimes online and are easy as well. His lectures are entertaining but hard to understand overall a goodprof tho.

Its not a difficult class but ppldont show up bc hw is simple fill in blank code n it sneaks up on exams. take an hour to bullet point readings so you dont have to start from scratch w 16 pages of his study guides. exams 50 - 75 MCQ w cheat sheet. He is funny and chill abt giving second chances for assignments and extending due dates or quizzes.

Funniest professor I have seen on campus! Quizzes are open notes. 2 pages of notes on Exams. The real problem is that the exam questions are confusing. He rewords them to the point where it becomes difficult to remember where a concept comes from. I wouldn't say this class is easy to get an A, but he wouldn't let his students fail either.

I finished this class over summer. Overall pretty easy as long as you do well on Labs and Quizzes. He has a bright energy that keeps us awake especially early over summer. Exams were 50% of ur grade- 40+ questions of T or F style with cheat sheets. Id take him again

his lectures r just him reading off of pdf's he made. his coding assignments r based on windows tutorials on web design. his exams were the hardest part bc i feel like they weren't rlly based on what he taught, u would have to do extra research to know the answers. maybe i would take him again if he actually lectured but it made it easy to skip

His class covers HTML, CSS, JavaScript, etc., with labs, code labs, quizzes, and exams. Labs are manageable and highly recommended; code labs, though ungraded, are essential. Lectures focus on concepts, not coding. Exams allow cheat sheets and consist of a lot of code. Professor is unlike any other, definitely a professor you should take

He's ok, puts in more effort and energy than most profs here. Kinda hard to understand and has a few quirks that makes lectures a little tiring sometimes. Tests are also designed pretty terribly but overall can't complain too much since allows 2 pages of notes and overall is a friendly guy.

Phong is a good guy, if you do bad on the tests just do well on the labs and quizzes. Cares a lot about his students and is always willing to help. Out of all the professors at CSULB for CS, he's one of the good ones, please respect him. Bad reviews are just from ppl that didn't take the class seriously but the class is doable/easy.

The class can be boring if they're all quiet and don't engage in the class because he just reads lecture notes mostly words for words. But in 1 on 1, he's very chill and easy going. I appreciate that he gives study guide similar to exam, which helps me A LOT. Code hw=fill in partial mostly. Quiz=open notes. The class was do-able.
Bro save yourself from this class. Literally he is so bad.

He retells the same jokes about sexual harassment and marijuana. It makes attending class uncomfortable. His lectures are a waste of time because he just reads word-for-word from the code labs provided by the Google for Developers course "Android Basics with Compose." Exams are T/F style questions copied straight from the code labs.

He is a great professor! The main reason he is great is that his lectures are entertaining, filled with jokes that he keep saying all the time. It kinds of gets boring when he just reads through the codelabs and you don't really learn much from his lectures. If you want to to laugh at his jokes during the lectures, I suggest you take him.
Everyday, I strive to be like Phuong Nguyen. What a fantastic person and professor.

I don't like the way he teaches the class. .NET is an interesting topic but I feel like I didn't learn as much as I could've with a better professor. Labs were to easy and it was mostly copying what he explained, not actually figuring it out by yourself.

Class covers a lot of topics, imo too much. It's all about C# and .NET env. Teacher is a personality himself, you have to get used to it. Overall a good guy, but sometimes a bit unclear. Class contains a lot of labs, which I highly recommend doing - helps you to understand the material. Material should be updated, be sure to be reading it yourself.

Professor Nguyen is one of the funniest professors in the cs dept. His lectures and notes are often just regurgitating Microsoft documentation, but his random comments make it entertaining. Exams were mc with a cheat sheet, sometimes questions word for word from the notes. Easy course and lots of important technologies used in industry.

This course is no longer offered, but his lectures are useful and funny. He wants his students to succeed and learn. The course consisted of weekly lab assignments (attendance required to demo labs), 4 quizzes (lowest dropped), 3 exams.

Phuon was not to bad but the course wasn't great. Text to speech from the book most of the class for 343 but all the material is good to keep and reuse after the semester is over. A lot of his Summer 343 course is learning on your own and if you are someone who is stuck to a professor's lessons then go take the class in reg sessions.

As a person he's pretty chill and the class is an easy A. The issue is that he is a useless professor. The majority of the lectures consisted of him clicking "text to speech" on highlighted sections of the textbook and LinkedIn videos. He would also occasionally compliment himself that he's a "good professor". He doesn't teach so don't expect much.

Weekly labs. Starter code & 5 20-page links/guides but unclear/incorrect directions, ends up being double the work just to figure out what you need to do. Gave SG but made changes the day before exam. Refuses to answer any questions, views it as you-should-know or interrupting. Goes off-topic & over-time. Funny & nice but not the greatest prof imo.

I will admit that he taught Nathan Pickrell (lab leader). Phuong was so funny and cracks jokes before COVID happened. We did the ATM project. Which we went over sequence diagrams, UMLs, and wrote in python. first exam was hard, but I did better on the other exams. Most questions of 343 were searchable. Bc of COVID, he was more lenient on grading

This is a great professor to take for an easy A. This class isn't necessarily easy, but Nguyen is very lenient with when you turn in assignments plus his lecture notes which he posts online are super helpful with labs. The tests aren't too bad either. He's also hilarious. Overall highly recommend.

HILARIOUS, RIDICULOUS, CARING. Don't let his offputting strict asian dad demeanor fool you. Almost didn't take him bc of that but I'm glad I did. Due to COVID, gave everyone 100% on rest of labs. Test heavy (mult choice + coding), uploads lectures (ur tests arebased on these), flexible with lab deadlines (be vocal about it), super nice. Luv Phuong!

Super nice and funny. He really wants the best for us and wants us to succeed. Only problem is that he's not good at teaching. He'll just read word for word off of the lecture notes or slides. I don't go to class for the lectures, but I go to class for his jokes and to laugh. Sometimes it can be hard to understand what he is saying.

He curves the tests and the final grade. He is one of the funniest professors that I have ever had. He has a lot of energy which is good. He is one of the few professors that understands you should be learning so you can get a job, not just for a grade. His tests are mostly writing code and he drops the lowest quiz. He is a caring professor.

He is a funny professor who keeps the class focused using his humor during lectures. If you read and understand the lecture notes that he posts on his website, then you should be able to do the lab assignments.

Phuong Nguyen is by far one of the funniest professors you will ever meet at CSULB. Im glad we have him in our CECS department. Lectures notes are posted daily on his website. His lab assignments are designed to be tricky. It forces you to ask him questions to help you design an efficient program. 2 Midterms and a Final. 5 Quizzes, Drops 2.

An awesome professor. He lectures a lot from powerpoints. There are labs every week. They start off being difficult but transition to being pretty simple. Took 5 quizzes and he dropped the two lowest scores. There were two midterms and a final. He makes really funny jokes. If you laugh and make friendly conversation with him you'll do fine.

In my experience this professor made the lectures engaging. Although he was not the best at handing back assignments on time, it is understandable because he was going through some personal stuff the semester I took him. As long as you attend lecture you will pass.

The class was actually pretty difficult. I struggled to get the labs done on time but he's pretty lenient on the due dates and it's usually extended anyway. The hardest part of the class are probably the exams which require you to memorize a lot of the code from the labs which is something that I couldn't really do. Better off teaching yourself.

Well well well... if I could give this man a hot pepper I would. Very nice and caring guy. He will help you with anything and everything. Good energy keeps you awake and focused in class. Exams are hard but he curves them. If I could take him for all my cecs classes I would.

He has really good energy and is super funny. His good energy helps with paying attention. His tests were extremely tough. He curves the tests. There were lots of projects and he kept changing the requirements for the projects. He gives lots of projects but is not strict with due dates. He wants you to learn the material so you can find a job.
Funny & nice, really good lectures except that he goes overtime pretty much everyday, but he's a good teacher & I would take him again.

Really good professor, knows his subject. He wants the student not only to succeed at school but also to be prepared for professional life. That's why he will make lectures sometimes last longer than the usual lecture time. He is really flexible on due dates also, because he wants you to finish the projects and understand the hot points.
Hottest professor in the CS department. He deserves that hot pepper rating! Yummers!
Tests are fair and curved. He is flexible with due dates. Keeps me awake in class, has a lot of energy.

Chill and funny guy. Lax on due dates. No hw just labs. Some quizzes. Do the labs and understand it. Some midterm coding questions are directly from parts of the labs. Read the posted lecture ppt for midterm too. Overall, this class was not too bad. Just understand the labs and lecture ppts and you should be gucci. Attendence not mandatory :).

I took both 277 and 282 above with this guy (this review also for 282). To get an A, take good notes AND review them constantly, do the labs AND review them, and read (only for 277). Midterms and quizzes are based on the slides (277) or files he gives you on his website (282) and his notes(both). Unstable effort in 282 got me a B, unfortunately.

Difficult to rate this class because I feel like the content of this class could be the best Ive had so far. However, his teaching ability is another story as he lacks the ability to present the material in a productive way. He heavily refers to online resources and tutorials and expects memorizing syntax that has been barely taught.

Takes his job very seriously and cares more about you understanding the material than the grade you get. I felt like the classes I took with him were challenging, but not so hard you're worried about failing. Has a bit of an accent but you get used to it. Overall he is a nice guy and the class is doable as long as you put in the work.

He does not teach this course, he simply provides you the material to learn. Entire class will be self-learning. Exams are largely memorization of code from the various assignments he's given you. The code to some assignments can be found on PDF's he gives you. You'd be better off just learning .NET on your own, on your own time. Take another prof.
Test are based on how much random code you can memorize.  Lectures are not good.  It is a barely okay class, but take something or someone else if you can.

His style of lecturing gives me anxiety. It's just too much. He's always yelling in really poor English basically just explaining what's on the board. His lectures would be much better if he just explained what's going on without all the awkward unnecessary "what?" he throws into each sentence. He should not try so hard and simply present info.
His lectures are great because you are always laughing and that makes them easier to follow. You have to do your job just like any other class. Study and you'll have a good grade.
Nice guy, sometimes unclear but overall, tried his best to keep you going. He's very relax on due dates and assignments are easy, no projects and exams are from PowerPoint, read the book for exams.

So intially you will think this guy is funny, but then you will soon find out how annoying that it is. He will stop mid sentence every other sentence and say what.  He just reads off the board and honestly might as well not even go to class. Does not do the labs himself so when problems happen he does not know how to help.
He will just read from the book.  Be prepared to here the word what.

He is very accommodating to assignments and cares for your best interest. He wants you to graduate with the tools it takes to land a job. The class has been very helpful and touches on many technologies used in industry today.
He's the best of the best and he knows it. He should be the star in an action comedy film. He'd definitely win an Oscar.

Professor Nguyen's philosophy is that the purpose of school is to help you get a job.  Accordingly, he focuses on practical applications rather than theory.  He's patient and easy to talk to, and he'll give you a lot of guidance on assignments if he thinks you need it.  No textbook, just notes. One of the better instructors I've had at CSULB.

Phuong is a great professor and is always there if you need help.  He is not easy though.  Assignments can be very tedious and tough at some times.  In order to get a good grade on exams, you need to take good notes during lecture and read the book.  At the end, what he teaches does help you prepare you for future interviews for jobs.
I will not take him again

I have no idea how I ended up with my final grade. He's a great lecturer but his grading system makes NO sense. Lab criteria changes from start to finish. Not really clear what he expects from you on exams. Overall he's still one of the better professors at CSULB, just kind of strange.
He is funny guy.  Learn from your projects and understand the concepts.  His labs are not very dense except for the first few.

Great professor. Since you only take one C++ class at this school, he uses lab time to lecture to match the lecture time you'd receive at a UC. He is very mindful of what employers look for and indicates it throughout lecture. The tests can be difficult, but the curve is proportional and he is good at reviewing and telling you what to expect.

Great professor! He goes out of his way to make sure you learn as much as possible. The tests are no cakewalk, but he curves and is pretty clear about his expectations. He can be difficult to understand at first, but you get used to it. He teaches class like a professor who wants you to get a job and will give you extra information on how to do so.

Very good professor overall. Be prepared to do a lot of work for this class. He is very helpful, if you are stuck on something & very lenient on due dates as long as you show work. Only 2 exams plus final & 5 quizzes dropping the lowest score.

Very good professor. His English isn't perfect but it isn't an english class, you'll begin to understand him and he teaches really well. He's lenient on due dates, and he teaches you using a lot of examples rather than boring lecturing. Highly recommended.  He is clear, I am wish him.

Awesome professor! He's funny, reasonable and clear about his expectations. He extends the assignments deadline all the time too. His notes are good, but if you want to do well on the test you should read the textbook. The labs are tough, but not overly so. He allows a one-side cheat sheet for every test.

Since I knew Java, assignments were easy, but for people who do not, it may take time.  The midterm and final were long and required lots of studying.  Phuong is a good professor, it is just the concept that is a little difficult when it comes to Java.  Very helpful, generous and funny. Only complaint is that he talks a little fast.
Very helpful prof. he makes some jokes to keep things interesting at times but his lecture notes and his teaching is very clear and easy to follow.

One of my favorite professors, extremely fair minded, and extremely clear on expectations. Although it was a morning class, he was hilarious enough to keep me awake for his entire lectures. The projects and tests are easy enough if you pay attention and take notes. Most of the time his notes are thorough enough that you do not need the book.

Great professor, I had him previously for cecs 100 as well. He teaches very clear, and actually spends time writing out the notes on the board, rather than using powerpoint. This way we can learn at a better pace, and if he makes mistakes we can correct him, which is a better approach to learning. Do the assignments and quizzes are exam are easy.

IF YOU ARE NOT AN ENGINEERING MAJOR DO NOT TAKE CECS 100. Don't get tricked to take this class for critical thinking. This is a hard class. Phuong Nguyen is the best of the best cecs teacher. He is pretty good but if you want an easy teacher take Professor Winter. He posts up lecture notes on his webpage. Use that to study for his quizzes and test.
Great professor but don't expect CECS 228 to be an easy subject, It is difficult even with a great teacher. study for the midterms and you will be fine

Great Professor. Sometimes this class could be difficult with all the proofs. He tries to make sure that everyone understand what hes teaching and really seems to care for his students. Sometimes class could get a little boring but sometimes he tells random story or says something funny to grab your attention again.
the person below me made the best post of all time.
He is clear to me, I am wish him.
Now I can actually say he is the best of the best!! really good professor, very helpful and knows how to teach! He is funny too, likes to say "yo mama"  a lot!

Really good teacher, he is super Korean but at the end of the semester I could finally understand him, projects are super easy. He gives most the code in lecture. Just take notes. He is also from Auburn, CA which makes him way cooler.
He's a good teacher. The tests are easy if you do the group work, since he essentially rehashes those problems onto his exams. Make sure you go to his lectures, as his notes are very helpful.

Phuong rocks. He will not be teaching 481 anymore (I think csulb not offering it anymore) however, he is very fair and can keep a 4 hour friday class entertaining. Material is cool, tests you should make really good notecards (6pt font) and study out of the book. Lab assignments dont take too long.

I didn't think it was possible for a teacher with such a heavy accent to be so effective. I was wrong. But I took him in 481 so he didn't hold back on his assignments. Fortunately, he is lenient on the due dates and lets us turn them in a day late if we're behind. Definitely one of the better CECS teachers.

Difficult to understand at times... he has a heavy accent and speaks quickly. He gives a lot of examples but I never got the sense of an overall picture. He didn't like the textbook, even though I felt I sometimes got more out of it than from him. He goes over alloted lecture time which cuts into (needed) lab time. Flexible turn in dates.
this guys baller he loves money baby! great teacher knows his stuff HW and projects are dense quiz and test are hard. but you learn your java like no other

I knew nothing about C++ when coming in, came out knowing so much. His test are hard, you need to study for them. Projects and labs seem overwhelming, lenient on due dates. If you get stuck offers help. Accent is hard to understand, you adjust. Funny and goes off on many tangents. Cares about his students. Grades on curve. Best CECS 174 teacher.
He is the best teacher I've ever had. His teaching method is very helpful. A lot of works though everything is from the lecture note. Funny guy.

This class is a lot of work there are a lab, homework and a project due every week.he gives extensions ;2 midterms very challenging but not impossible to get a A , and a very hard final exam. take Barbra Mack u'll work less harder for an A.

This is good if u understand how to program. I never got the hang of it, but then again i didnt read the book every week. Instead i crammed before each test. I ended up with an c- but that's b/c of the tests. Need to read the book and understand his lecture. Nice and funny guy.

I loved this class! Probably my favorite this semester. Excellent teacher. He explains everything thoroughly in lectures and then helps you in everyway possible when you're doing labs. Could have been a very boring class, but he made it fun. 2 exams and final, with ~30 MC questions and ~6 questions where you write coding

one of the best teacher in cecs department, he makes sure that everyone can understand the material before he moves on, provides good examples and explanations. he has an accent but after few classes you will get used to it, he's very funny and cheerful person. wish he thought every class in cecs department.

I only with he taught every CECS class in the department. His teaching methods are very good. He's very peppy and energetic, and if your class meets on halloween, you will be in for a treat. He's one of the most helpful professors out there and he makes the subject matter fun to study.

The first couple of classes you can't understand his accent and feel like you need to answer his rhetorical "what" when he can't find the word to say. BUT after getting used to it, he is awesome at explaining the material, uses great examples and makes sure everyone understands before moving on. Great teacher!
He is the best lecturer in programming classes. He made the materials easier and simplier to understand. Very helpful in labs.

Easily one of the best professors I've ever had.  Intelligent, hilarious, and explains the material well, with plenty of examples.  You may have trouble understanding him at first, but that's part of the whole Phoung experience!

I wish i would teach every single CECS class he is the best teacher ever. very sincere, generous, clear , but dont take advantage of him. he is pationate about his work and explains really really well.
very rude and condescending...he will not help in most instances and will tell you to look things up for yourself when you ask questions.

funny guy, but his jokes gets played out. deep accent, kinda hard to understand. the labs and tests are easy, pretty much gave away the answer. but i can't stand his lame jokes that he says over and over.
Funny guy, his lectures are helpful for lab. If you understand the lab, his tests are easy.
THE best teacher in the CECS dept. Funny but the jokes get too old at times. Use one side/page notes during exam. TIP: copy all lab assignments in a page. + plus notes.

Phoung Nguyen, super funny guy. He got an accent but you will get used to it. His labs are really easy if you are really paying attention to his note, the answer is in front of you. He class would be an easy A if you pay attention to the lecture.

at first he is a bit difficult to understand but u will get use to it.. he is a funny professor and very helpful . he is a very intellectual man. i definately recommend him. very good teacher. makes JAVA fun
He is very funny and a nice guy. He has an accent but you get used to it after a while. His labs were easy but his tests take a bit of effort to get an A. A very good teacher. Highly recommend him!

Fun class, the projects were neat, but hard. He gives a lot of examples during lecture.  He has strange way of speaking, it takes a few weeks to be able to really understand what hes saying. Lots of amusing anicdotes, funny guy.

funny guy, hard to understand first two weeks, but u'll get over it..  true that he's an easy A.. but u'll learn a lot while ur in his class..  1pg cheat sheet for midterms and 2pgs for final..  juss cut 'n paste programs onto cheat sheet 'n u'll be fine
Good teacher. Explains java really well, and practically writes the labs for you from the notes. Easy A.
great teacher. funny and serious. made java easy to understand. :)
He's really cool, just be cool and he'll be cool back.  It was hard to understand what he was saying the first few weeks but you get use to it, he made java much simpler than my other java teacher.
Phuong Nyguen you will hear that plenty. A super funny person and can not help laughing at his jokes and stores and his accent.  Helpful in the labs, but office hours and e-mails forget about it
